text.p: Modem maker U.S. Robotics Corp said Friday it was eliminating "a couple of hundred" jobs. It declined to specify what areas of the company would be affected.
"In terms of actual elimination of positions, it's a couple of hundred of people," said Karen Novak, spokeswoman for the Skokie, Ill.- based company. "It's a process of managing our growth."
Novak said the company is also laying off people for performance reasons, but those positions could be refilled.
U.S. Robotics's fiscal year ended September 30, and the company does employee performance evaluations at year-end.
"We've let people go for performance reasons," Novak told Reuters.
U.S. Robotics employs about 6,000 people. Novak said the number losing their jobs would not reach 10 percent, or 600.
"It's not more than single digit (percent) of overall headcount," she said.
Analysts said the number of job cuts was small compared to the 3,000 new jobs created at the company during the past year.
"I think it is about 100 to 200, nothing major," said Amar Senan, analyst for Volpe, Welty & Co.
He believes the job cuts are mainly on production lines.
"To put it in perspective, they've added about 3,000 people in fiscal '96," Senan said.
